periods.market_context: The 2023-2024 period was a year of payback to insurance-linked securities (ILS) investors and the reinsurance market. ILS market returns in 2022 were down due to spread widening and Hurricane Ian, but those losses were largely recouped in 2023 and the positive performance continued into 2024. Returns were aided by an absence of any major catastrophes during the period.
periods.thesis: The manager's thesis involved reinvestment of maturity proceeds into a much more favourable spread environment and benefiting from spread tightening. The strategy also focused on actively managing risk, specifically reducing exposure to Florida Hurricane risk while maintaining portfolio spreads generally at, or above 1000bps and reducing the expected loss of the fund.
periods.decisions_taken:
There were a significant number of changes to the underlying holdings. The fund continued to reduce its exposure to Florida Hurricane risk. Florida Hurricane remained the dominant exposure, while Texas Hurricane took over from California Earthquake as the second biggest exposure. periods.observed_outcome: The Fund’s NAV (USD Accumulation Class) saw performance from June 2023 to June 2024 rise by 12.5%. This outperformed the EurekaHedge ILS Index, which returned 12.0% over the same period. The returns were primarily driven by reinvestment of maturity proceeds into a much more favourable spread environment and the portfolio benefiting from spread tightening at certain points in the period.
periods.notes: The manager anticipates portfolio spreads will likely tighten as investors receive coupon interest and seek to put that money to work in the secondary markets. There is also talk of investors profit taking ahead of the hurricane season due to forecasts for severe activity, which could offset coupon-driven demand. However, spread changes during the summer are expected to have little impact on post-hurricane spreads in a normal season.
